drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: Code Generation with Claude Code scenario. A team's monorepo has test files in every package
drills.answer_line: SAM: Forty copies that drift, and every new package starts with none.
drills.stem: A monorepo has test files in every package. Testing conventions sit in the root CLAUDE.md, so they load in every session. The team wants them to load only when Claude works on a test file. What should they do?

options.A: Add a CLAUDE.md with the testing conventions to every directory that contains tests
options.B: Move them to a .claude/rules file with a paths frontmatter field of **/*.test.tsx
options.C: Ask each developer to move the conventions into their own user-level CLAUDE.md
options.D: Turn the conventions into a skill that developers invoke before writing tests

drills.why: One glob rule covers every test file and loads only on contact. Per-directory copies drift; user level misses new hires; a skill depends on remembering.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Code Generation with Claude Code scenario. Two developers on the same repository
drills.answer_line: SAM: Miss pattern three: "first step" read as "most effective".
drills.stem: Two developers on the same repository report that Claude follows the team's error-handling convention in one developer's sessions and not the other's. What should the architect do first?

options.A: Run /memory in both developers' sessions and compare which memory files are loaded
options.B: Rewrite the convention in capitals with an example
options.C: Add a PreToolUse hook that blocks edits which break the convention
options.D: Move both developers to a larger model

drills.why: "First": same repo, different behaviour points to differing config, likely a user-level file. Diagnose before you build; C skips the diagnosis.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. Code Generation with Claude Code scenario. A team's codebase-impact skill
drills.answer_line: SAM: Both. A answers "buries the session"
drills.stem: Choose two. A codebase-impact skill needs the module name, but developers often invoke it with no arguments and get a vague result. When it runs, it reads dozens of files and buries the session. Which two frontmatter changes address these problems?

options.A: Add context: fork so the analysis runs in an isolated sub-agent context
options.B: Add an argument-hint so developers are prompted for the module name
options.C: Add allowed-tools listing the shell tool so the skill can search faster
options.D: Move the skill's instructions into the root CLAUDE.md so they are always available
options.E: Add a line to the skill body asking Claude to keep its output short

drills.why: A answers "buries the session"; B answers "invoked with no arguments". C widens access and fixes neither; D loads a task workflow into every session.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Code Generation with Claude Code scenario. A platform team writes Terraform
drills.answer_line: SAM: A. One glob catches every Terraform file wherever it lives
drills.stem: Terraform lives in an infra folder and in each service's deploy subfolder. The team wants its Terraform conventions applied whenever Claude edits any Terraform file, and loaded at no other time. What is the best approach?

options.A: A .claude/rules file with a paths field matching **/*.tf
options.B: A CLAUDE.md in the infra folder containing the conventions
options.C: A section in the root CLAUDE.md headed "when editing Terraform"
options.D: A skill that developers run before editing Terraform

drills.why: One glob catches every Terraform file and loads only then. B misses the deploy folders; C loads every session; D relies on someone remembering.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. Developer Productivity with Claude scenario. A team's agent has a code-search
drills.answer_line: SAM: Both. B fixes the description that loses to Grep
drills.stem: Choose two. The agent uses Grep instead of the code-search MCP tool for tracing callers, and makes 15 exploratory calls to discover table structures before every query. Which two changes address the root causes?

options.A: Expose the database schemas as an MCP resource so the agent sees available data without exploring
options.B: Expand the code-search tool's description: capabilities, outputs, when to use it instead of Grep
options.C: Remove Grep from the agent's tools
options.D: Raise the agent's maximum number of turns so the exploration finishes
options.E: Replace both servers with a single custom server that combines them

drills.why: B fixes the description that loses to Grep; A removes the need to explore. C is a blunt cut, D pays for the symptom, E is over-engineering.
